title: Rediff Files Updated IPO Papers For ₹600 Cr Fresh Issue-Only IPO
summary: Rediff files updated draft IPO papers with SEBI for a Rs 600 crore fresh issue
detailed: With the IPO, Rediff, which is one of India’s earliest internet portals and digital media companies, intends to raise ₹600 Cr via a fresh issue of shares.
A large part of the capital raised via the IPO will go towards expanding three businesses — enterprise solutions platform Rediff One; digital payments offering Rediff Pay; video platform Rediff TV.
Rediff has earmarked ₹224.8 Cr for capital expenditure across the three businesses — ₹94.5 Cr on Rediff One, ₹64.3 Cr on Rediff Pay and ₹66 Cr on Rediff TV.
In digital media, Rediff operates Rediff News and Rediff TV, alongside its homepage.
sentences: With the IPO, Rediff, which is one of India’s earliest internet portals and digital media companies, intends to raise ₹600 Cr via a fresh issue of shares.
The company had confidentially filed its IPO papers in April 2026, with an estimated issue size of ₹600-800 Cr.
A large part of the capital raised via the IPO will go towards expanding three businesses — enterprise solutions platform Rediff One; digital payments offering Rediff Pay; video platform Rediff TV.
Rediff has earmarked ₹224.8 Cr for capital expenditure across the three businesses — ₹94.5 Cr on Rediff One, ₹64.3 Cr on Rediff Pay and ₹66 Cr on Rediff TV.
Another ₹183.34 Cr will be used to fuel marketing and branding while the remaining proceeds will be used for acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

For context, Ajit Balakrishnan founded the company in 1996 with a host of digital services like email services, shopping, news, etc, Rediff has evolved significantly into a tech-led business under the AvenuesAI umbrella.
Balakrishnan retired in 2024 after Infibeam (now AvenuesAI) acquired a majority stake in the company.
Infibeam’s chairman Vishal Mehta took over as Rediff’s MD in October 2024.
As of now, the company operates across two broader segments: Consumer Digital Platforms (B2C) and Enterprise Digital Platforms (B2B).
Breaking this down further, Rediff operates four primary services in the B2C arena.
Its flagship email platform, Rediffmail has 152.46 Mn cumulative registered users as of September 30, 2026.
This includes all accounts created since the service was launched in 1998.
In digital media, Rediff operates Rediff News and Rediff TV, alongside its homepage.
The platforms offer current affairs, business information, editorial and video content.
Together, they had 90.83 Mn annual active users (AAUs), with an average visit duration of 321 seconds, as of September 2026.
Rediff TV, launched in July 2025, is still in the early stages of its business cycle.
The company also operates MoneyWiz, its personal finance information platform, which provides financial news and market data.
It had approximately 7.89 Mn AAUs at the end of the September quarter.
Its newest consumer offering is Rediff Pay, facilitates bill payments, P2P transfers, merchant payments through QR codes, and mobile and DTH recharges.
Having initially been available to a closed user group, Rediff Pay has transitioned to its full-service phase post NPCI’s TPAP approval.
On the B2B side, Rediff offers its products under the Rediff One brand.
The suite includes Rediffmail Enterprise for business email, rCloud for cloud storage, and Rediff Bol for enterprise messaging.
It also operates Rediff Commerce, an ecommerce enablement platform acquired through a business transfer agreement from AvenuesAI.

The platform helps small and mid-sized businesses build and manage online marketplaces, offering tools for storefront creation, catalogue management, payment integration, inventory, logistics and analytics.
It also incorporates AI-assisted features for product categorisation and catalogue optimisation.
Rediff plans to expand these offerings using IPO proceeds.

Its proposed initiatives include integrating enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM) and human resource management system (HRMS) modules into Rediff One, expanding Rediff Pay’s payments stack, developing Rediff TV into a broader streaming platform and increasing marketing investments.
Rediff reported a net profit of ₹35.2 Cr in the first quarter of FY27 on a top line of ₹58.4 Cr.
For the June 2026 quarter, EBITDA (excluding other income) stood at ₹39.43 Cr, translating into a margin of 67.54%.
For the full fiscal year FY26, the company’s operating revenue rose 258.7% to ₹133.6 Cr from ₹37.2 Cr in FY25.
Its net profit surged almost 9X YoY to ₹55.9 Cr from ₹5.9 Cr in the previous fiscal year.
EBITDA, excluding other income, stood at ₹65.24 Cr in FY26, compared with a loss of ₹4.29 Cr in FY25.
Its EBITDA margin improved to 48.83% from a negative 11.53% over the same period.
The company’s net debt stood at ₹261.48 Cr as of March 31, 2026, rising to ₹354.95 Cr by June 30, 2026.
Meanwhile, operating cash flow turned positive at ₹160.5 Cr in FY26, compared with an outflow of ₹61.29 Cr in FY25.
